Strengths and costs

Working in its favor
  • 101 feet of waterfront with tidelands, medium bank
  • County rates the views: Puget Sound excellent, Olympics good
  • Public sewer and water at the street
  • County marks the lot buildable
  • Direct road access, with the building area between the road and the beach
  • It had a house before, with its own address and stairs
  • County values the land at $1,331,000
What will cost time or money
  • Steep and heavily treed. County lists 45% as unusable, and part of the lot is beach and tidelands
  • Steep slope area, with a slide repair on record from 2003
  • The old house is gone. Only a collapsed platform is left
  • No rock wall visible along the beach on this lot
  • One-lane gravel road, tight for trucks and equipment
  • Shoreline and tree rules will apply
  • Easements on the lot, not yet reviewed

Open questions

Four things to confirm

  1. Can two homes go on this lot, either by splitting it or by building two on one lot?
  2. What does a foundation on this kind of slope cost per home?
  3. Would the city require road improvements or a shoreline wall?
  4. With the old house gone, does the right to build close to the water still apply?

A walkthrough of the lot can be arranged.
